issue_context.title: (Frivolous) Suggestion: Clean up empty lines in generated HTML
issue_context.body:
### Description

Vite, when generating HTML, will leave blank lines where script or link tags are removed for later replacement, for example:

> `input.html`
```
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
    <head>
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="/styles/global.css" />
    </head>
    <body>
        <script type="module" src="/index.jsx"></script>
    </body>
</html>
```

> `output.html`
```
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
    <head>
        
        <script type="module" crossorigin src="/index.5f98c88f.js"></script>
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/index.d0e1e89c.css">
    </head>
    <body>
        
    </body>
</html>
```

As tags are removed/replaced at their exact position start, extra whitespace can be left over post-build.

Whilst very frivolous, it would be nice if these blank lines were cleaned up afterwards.

### Suggested solution

This should suffice:

```js
processedHtml.set(id, s.toString().replace(/(^\s*\n\s*|\s*\n\s*$)/gm, ''))
```

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/1a2e5e6d9a6bb2531bf73be801c9778dbf39d51b/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/html.ts#L591

### Alternative

I don't believe there's any other (safe) alternatives. Removing extraneous whitespace after the fact is certainly far easier and less prone to error compared to altering all previous replacements and removals.

I suppose you could also just tell users to run `prettier` post build, but that's not ideal.

### Additional context

_No response_

review_comments: I think it'd nice to have a comment that this variable points the line break. Or change `node.sourceCodeLocation!.startCol` to `node.sourceCodeLocation!.startCol - 1`, so that it points the 0-indexed line start.

Sure

> Or change `node.sourceCodeLocation!.startCol` to `node.sourceCodeLocation!.startCol - 1`, so that it points the 0-indexed line start.

Not quite sure I follow, columns are not 0-indexed. Add a `- 1` and you're pointing to the previous line.

I mean I think `lineStartOffset` points the line break in the previous line in the code of this PR.
```html
<!-- -->
<script></script>
```
In this example HTML, the values are:
- `node.sourceCodeLocation!.startOffset` (0-indexed): 1
- `node.sourceCodeLocation!.startCol` (1-indexed): 1
- `lineStartOffset` (0-indexed): 0 (the line break in the previous line)

If `lineStartOffset` is changed like below, `lineStartOffset` will point the start of the line.
```js
const lineStartOffset =
  node.sourceCodeLocation!.startOffset -
  (node.sourceCodeLocation!.startCol - 1) // convert to 0-index
```

Sorry, deleted my first response as I misread.

~~I'm not sure what the point is in the change? Sure, you could point to the newline and change the regex, but that doesn't offer anything that I'm aware of?~~

Edit: I'm not sure that would be correct without revising every subsequent tag insertion? We want to remove the newline

What I was suggesting is that if this variable (`lineStartOffset`) is pointing to a newline, then either

- Clarify in the comment that it is pointing to the line break in the previous line
  - I think the current comment (`Gets the offset for the start of the line that the node is on`) is missing the information that it's pointing to the line break.
- Change the code to point to the beginning of the line instead of the line break in the previous line, so that the variable name is correct

I'd consider the newline part of the "line", hence the name -- when you insert a new tag into an HTML (especially in the head) you'd always append a newline to the end of the previous. The newline at the end of one element is in all practicality the line start for the next element.

But if you want it changed I can do that I suppose.

Edit: Updated it, if you prefer it say something else please make a suggestion & we can apply that. More efficient than trying to guess what you're after / matches the project conventions.
Ah, I see. That makes sense as well. Thank you!
